title.narrative: Outreach Programme - Widening the Engagement. To offer quality content engaging the Myanmar public on critical issues relevant to Myanmar and the country’s future, and to model the values espoused by U Thant.
The accessibility and outreach of contents through the website, Facebook and Instagram. The metrics used by (number of followers, engagement on articles, reach and influence., etc)

target.value: Maintain and improve the www.LostFootsteps.org website aiming at producing 6-12 well researched articles and interactive maps, focusing on content that can contribute to today's discussions on Myanmar’s future including messages on diversity, economic policies and the environment, making global comparisons.

actual.value: 10 researched articles, 4 short visuals-driven posts finalized and posted on the www.LostFootsteps.org website; Several articles are still in progress. The www.LostFootsteps.org website had reached an audience of a total 825,713 users (54,812 new users in 2022) and a readership (page views) of 1,868,508 (164,650 views in 2022) by end of December 2022. • Launched LostFootsteps Instagram page in April 2022; posted hundreds of posts reached over 200,000 Instagram users. Gained over 5,000 followers and reached 218,000 accounts, and the number of followers had grown to 9,134 by end of December. Continued maintenance, troubleshooting and improvements. Continued impact and reach, despite a changing political environment. However, the number of users of the www. has been significantly lower compared to the years before the military coup in February 2021, due to the security situation and internet and social media accessibility and restrictions since then.

title.narrative: Heritage Programme - Honouring U Thant’s Legacy. Operating the property and premises of U Thant House as a centre for research, learning and dialogue, ensuring that the site continues to remain under the stewardship of U Thant House as an organization, and that the premises are maintained in a way that it is safe for visitors and offers an environment conducive for the work programmes we are operating, including functioning as an effective workplace and office for the staff supporting our overall work programme.

The U Thant House property and its premises continue to be under the stewardship of the organization U Thant House, remains well maintained and in condition to serve as a centre for research, learning and dialogue and a functioning office for staff supporting our work programmes.

target.value: Continued upkeep and maintenance of the property as a centre for research, learning and dialogue, safe for visitors and staff.

actual.value: A team of caretakers and gardeners have continued with the basic upkeep and maintenance of UTH and ensured that the property and its premises are in good shape to open to visitors and a functioning office for staff supporting the programs.

title.narrative: Research & Dialogue Programme – Informing Policy. To respond to Myanmar’s political, economic, and humanitarian crises by developing fresh ideas and identifying creative solutions, through targeted research and ongoing dialogue.
Ideas developed by U Thant House are discussed by policymakers in Myanmar and internationally.

target.value: Maintain contacts and connections with Myanmar civil society and political leaders and scholars; provide analysis and advice and participate in private discussions as requested. Continue close monitoring of political- and political economy developments in Myanmar and support as appropriate United Nations and other diplomatic and humanitarian efforts to protect and assist Myanmar civilians and ameliorate the current crisis. Encourage continued international attention to the crisis in Myanmar and provide analysis to leaders, officials, and scholars in Europe and elsewhere.

actual.value: Continued monitoring political- and political economy developments. Encouraged continued international attention to the crisis in Myanmar and provided analysis to leaders, officials, and scholars. Completed advanced drafts of six (6) Discussion Notes/Background Briefs on social development policy, agricultural policy, etc. Progress had been made with the research project to study UN’s mediation and the role of UN Special Envoys in Myanmar up to 2016. Preliminary desk research was also undertaken for the period of 2016-2021, and for the new envoy in 2022.

title.narrative: Museum & Education Programme – Inspiring Future Generations. To broaden the horizons of youth and young adults in Myanmar by encouraging new thinking and introducing critical issues not sufficiently covered in the national curriculum (peace and tolerance and the need to safeguard our natural environment), and to model the values U Thant espoused and encourage reflection on how they apply to students’ daily lives in terms of upholding human dignity, challenging prejudice, and promoting nonviolence, and caring for the earth.

• Maintained museum and exhibition open to the public with skilled guides/learning facilitators engaging the visitors. • Developed educational materials and activities on peace and tolerance and sustainable environment for students

target.value: Completion of education materials and lesson plans targeted at youth and young adults 16+ on the themes of peace, tolerance, democracy, human rights and the need to care for our environment through sustainable development. All student resource materials (targeted at primary/ secondary students and 16+) will be finalized for dissemination; proofread, designed and laid out and translated from English to Burmese. Security situation and public health situation permitting, dissemination of materials will start in the second half of 2022. The combined packages of education materials targeted at different age groups of students, will mean that UTH is well prepared to offer exciting education programmes to visitors as soon as the situation permits.

actual.value: Due to the coup in February 2021, and the present security situation in Myanmar, UTH has closed most of the year and reopened in December 2022. The targets on Museum and Education Programme works achieved far lower than planned activities: • The education materials and ‘lesson plans’ for youth and young adults (16+) continued up until April 2022, but not been making progress since. • The museum exploratory re-opened at the end of December 2022 just for donor/partners and diplomatic community. In 2022, three local staffs and one international education consultant left UHT, and no recruitment has made so far, which was also one of the reasons of poor outcomes.

title.narrative: Contributing ideas and fresh thinking on policy options for Myanmar’s future – reimagine peace and rethink (economic) development. Contributing to ensuring continued engagement on Myanmar in key capitals around the world and shaping the international response to the political situation in Myanmar – of importance to Myanmar’s future.

Ideas originating from U Thant House are influencing political debates among (i) a selected set of domestic Myanmar actors (sensitive to the changing political landscape and carefully considering the safety of staff), and (ii) policy makers in key capitals around the world, shaping the international response to the political situation in Myanmar – of important to Myanmar’s future.

target.value: UTH will continue to advocate on political economy, poverty and vulnerability, multilateralism, China, and climate change.

actual.value: UTH continues to serve as a centre for research, learning and dialogue and continue to advocate on political economy, poverty and vulnerability, multilateralism, China. The U Thant House has: • Carried out research projects and continued to be devoted to adapting to external environment, managing financial and political risks. • Completed several substantive discussion notes/background briefs and research reports on Myanmar's political economy and related topics. • Continued to deliver on the lostfootsteps.org website and social media (Facebook & Instagram) including producing new contents on selected topics • Made progress to complete the education materials for Myanmar students and the general public. • Supported international high-level decision makers around the world, in virtual as well as in-person meetings. • Managed to maintain as a legal Myanmar entity, protect financial and other assets, and safeguard the site itself with adequate security and necessary upkeep and
